question: From an outside point P, two tangents, PA and PB, are drawn to a circle. Given that the length of PA is 12 cm, what is the length of PB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the tangent property of a circle, the lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are always equal.

⇒ Length of Tangent PA = Length of Tangent PB

⇒ PB = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of tangent PA = 12 cm.

PA and PB are tangents from an external point P to a circle with center O.

**Concept Used:**

A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency. By proving the two triangles formed by the tangents, radii, and the line connecting the external point to the center are congruent, we can establish that the tangent lengths are equal.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Consider △OAP and △OBP:

⇒ OA = OB (Radii of the same circle)

⇒ OP = OP (Common hypotenuse)

⇒ ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)

⇒ By RHS (Right angle - Hypotenuse - Side) congruence criterion, △OAP ≅ △OBP.

⇒ Therefore, PA = PB (Corresponding parts of congruent triangles)

⇒ Since PA = 12 cm, it follows that PB = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

When two circles do not intersect, the length of their direct common tangent is given by √(d² − (R − r)²), where d is the distance between their centers and R, r are their radii.

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of the transverse common tangent (which crosses the line segment joining the centers) is calculated using the formula √(d² − (R + r)²).

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment and a secant segment are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, the square of the length of the tangent is equal to the product of the external secant part and the entire secant length (PT² = PA × PB).

Number of Tangents Rule

From an external point, exactly two tangents can be drawn to a circle. From a point on the circle, exactly one tangent can be drawn, and from a point inside the circle, zero tangents can be drawn.
